t.2.29.1: Then, having received his brother's most auspicious and welcome command, he went and quickly entered the dwelling of Suyajña.
t.2.29.2: Having saluted that brahmin, who was staying in the fire-chamber, Lakṣmaṇa said: "Friend, come here and behold the dwelling of one who performs what is hard to do."
t.2.29.3: Then, having quickly performed the twilight worship, he went with Saumitri and entered that delightful dwelling of Rāma, endowed with splendor.
t.2.29.4: Rāghava, with Sītā, approached with joined palms Suyajña, the knower of the Vedas, who had come, as one approaches a worshipped fire.
t.2.29.5: With choice armlets made of gold, with lovely earrings, with gems strung on golden threads, with upper-arm bands and with bracelets too…
t.2.29.6: Kākutstha honored him in return with many other jewels as well. Then Rāma, urged by Sītā, spoke to Suyajña.
t.2.29.7: Gentle one, take this necklace and this golden thread to your wife. And now, my friend, Sītā wishes to give you a girdle as well.
t.2.29.9: The elephant named Śatruṃjaya, which my maternal uncle gave to me, I give to you together with a thousand elephants, O best of the twice-born.
t.2.29.8: This couch, too, with its excellent coverlet and adorned with many kinds of jewels, Vaidehī wishes to bestow upon you.
t.2.29.10: Thus addressed by Rāma, Suyajña accepted that gift and pronounced auspicious blessings upon Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā.
t.2.29.11: Then Rāma, ever sweet of speech, spoke these words to his dear brother, the composed Saumitri, as Brahmā speaks to the lord of the thirty gods.
t.2.29.12: O Saumitri, summon Agastya and Kauśika, those two foremost of brāhmaṇas, and honor them with jewels, as one nourishes a crop with waters.
t.2.29.13: He who, devoted, waits upon Kausalyā with blessings, the teacher of the Taittirīyas, learned and versed in the Vedas.
t.2.29.14: O Saumitri, have a carriage and maidservants given to him, and silken garments too, until that twice-born one is satisfied.
t.2.29.15: Citraratha, the noble charioteer and counsellor, who has dwelt with us for a very long time, please him too with costly jewels, garments, and wealth.
t.2.29.17: Then Lakṣmaṇa, that tiger among men, himself gave that wealth to the foremost of brāhmaṇas, just as he had been told, like Dhanada, the giver of riches.
t.2.29.16: And, Saumitri, provide a thousand loads of śāli rice, two hundred fine draught oxen, and a thousand cows to supply him with relishes.
t.2.29.18: Then, having given abundant wealth to each one of his dependents, he spoke to the dependents who stood there, their voices choked with tears.
t.2.29.19: The dwelling of Lakṣmaṇa and this house of mine must each be kept from standing empty until my return.
t.2.29.20: Having spoken thus to all those grieving people who depended on him, he said this to the keeper of the treasury: "Let the wealth be brought." Then the dependents brought all of his wealth.
t.2.29.21: Then that tiger among men, together with Lakṣmaṇa, had that wealth distributed to the twice-born, to the young and the old, and to the needy.
t.2.29.22: There lived there a tawny-hued twice-born of the Gārgya clan, Trijaṭa by name; up to the fifth courtyard no one held him back.
t.2.29.23: Approaching the prince, Trijaṭa spoke these words: "I am penniless and have many sons, O illustrious prince. I live always in the forest by gleaning; look upon me with kindness."
t.2.29.25: Hastily, in his excitement, he wrapped that cloth around his waist, and, whirling his staff, he hurled it with all his strength, impelled by vehemence.
t.2.29.24: Then Rāma, in jest, said to him: “Not even one thousand of my cows has yet been given away by me. As far as you can hurl your staff, so much shall you obtain.”
t.2.29.26: And then Rāma, consoling that Gārgya, said: "You must surely not be angry, for this was only a jest of mine."
t.2.29.27: Then the great sage Trijaṭa, together with his wife, delighted at receiving the herd of cows, pronounced blessings upon the great-souled one that would increase his fame, strength, joy and happiness.
